title: Freya and the Ledger
premise: Noor Eastwick, a courier carrying coded orders for the collapsing Republic of Vessany, arrives in the river town of Haldenmere just before the army seizes it and its famous ledger workshop—the ledger holding every name the republic promised to protect. Sheltered by Freya, the ledger-keeper's daughter who has spent the war keeping her own loyalties hidden, Noor must finish transcribing and distributing the names before the requisition officers burn the workshop. As the two fall in love, Noor's coded orders are revealed to be an order of abandonment: the republic has decided the names are expendable. In the end, Noor chooses truth over duty, delivering the ledger's pages to the families themselves as the town burns, and escapes with Freya carrying nothing but the one page that bears their own names.
about_author: Lena Galloway is the pen name of a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing displaced-persons records in northern Europe. She writes historical fiction about the paperwork of war—the ledgers, manifests, and letters that outlive the people they name.

chapters.title: What the Saddlebag Holds
chapters.summary: Noor's POV. Noor crosses the flooded border road into Haldenmere carrying sealed dispatches and a false merchant's pass, measuring every possession by what can be abandoned in a ditch. A checkpoint near-miss establishes the stakes. Emotional beat: weary vigilance, the loneliness of a person who is only their cargo.

chapters.title: The Town That Measures in Ink
chapters.summary: Noor's POV, with a brief Freya interlude. Noor delivers the dispatches to the ledger workshop of Aldous Venn and glimpses the famous registry—thousands of names of the displaced and the promised. Freya catches Noor lingering too long over the open book. Emotional beat: first wonder, and the first crack in Noor's invisibility.

chapters.title: Freya of the Second Floor
chapters.summary: Freya's POV. Freya, who has spent the war forging clean papers for neighbors while her father kept official ledgers, sizes up the courier sleeping in the workshop's storeroom. She notices Noor's hands shake and leaves bread without a word. Emotional beat: guarded curiosity, the habit of protecting strangers.

chapters.title: Requisition Orders
chapters.summary: Noor's POV. Captain Ilsen of the army arrives with requisition papers: the workshop, the registry, and the town's grain are now state property. Aldous Venn protests and is quietly threatened. Noor realizes the dispatches they carried may relate to the seizure. Emotional beat: dread arriving in stamped, official language.

chapters.title: Names Weigh More Than Paper
chapters.summary: Freya's POV. Freya shows Noor the ledger's true purpose at night: not a tax record but a protection registry, names of people the republic swore to evacuate. Noor says nothing about the sealed second dispatch. Emotional beat: intimacy through shared secrecy, the beginning of trust.

chapters.title: The Captain's Courtesy
chapters.summary: Noor's POV. Captain Ilsen invites Noor to dinner, probing how much the courier knows, offering safe passage out in exchange for 'cooperation.' Noor deflects but learns the army plans to burn the workshop's archives within the month. Emotional beat: the seduction and danger of being seen.

chapters.title: Copying by Candlelight
chapters.summary: Alternating POV, chapter split in two. Noor and Freya begin secretly transcribing the registry by hand, page by page, hiding copies inside book bindings. The work is slow; the deadline is not. Emotional beat: purpose found in complicity, tenderness growing between shared labor.

chapters.title: The Informant's Debt
chapters.summary: Freya's POV. Freya discovers the workshop's apprentice, Tomas, has been reporting to Ilsen to pay off his family's debts. She confronts him and buys his silence with a forged discharge paper. Emotional beat: the corrupting arithmetic of survival—everyone is trading something.

chapters.title: Dispatch, Second Seal
chapters.summary: Noor's POV. Cornered by conscience, Noor finally opens the second dispatch: the republic has rescinded the evacuations. The names in the ledger are officially abandoned; Noor's orders are to certify the registry's destruction. Emotional beat: the floor dropping out—the mission was a lie of omission all along.

chapters.title: What Noor Does Not Say
chapters.summary: Freya's POV. Freya senses Noor carrying something terrible and mistakes it for wavering loyalty to the republic. They quarrel; Freya accuses Noor of being the army's errand runner. Emotional beat: love strained by the exact virtue that caused it—truth withheld to protect.

chapters.title: The River Route
chapters.summary: Noor's POV. Noor scouts an escape plan for the copied pages by barge and maps which families could still be warned in time, against orders. Ilsen's patrols tighten after a warehouse fire. Emotional beat: duty and conscience pulling in opposite directions, Noor leaning toward the fall.

chapters.title: Tomas Pays His Debt Differently
chapters.summary: Freya's POV. Tomas, wracked with guilt, reveals Ilsen has moved the burning up—ten days, not a month—and that Noor's name appears on the army's list of persons to detain. Emotional beat: betrayal repaid with warning; the clock becomes merciless.

chapters.title: Confession at the Binding Table
chapters.summary: Noor's POV. Noor tells Freya everything: the rescinded orders, the certification they were sent to sign, the lie of the mission. Freya's response is not forgiveness but a question—what will you do now? Emotional beat: the terrible relief of being fully known.

chapters.title: Ten Days of Paper
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. The transcription becomes a town conspiracy: the baker hides pages in flour sacks, the ferryman memorizes routes, Aldous Venn, broken but rallied, teaches them which names matter most. Emotional beat: a community choosing each other over safety.

chapters.title: Ilsen's Dinner, Second Course
chapters.summary: Noor's POV. Ilsen, suspecting the courier, presents Noor with the certification document and a pen, offering again to look away if Noor signs and leaves. Noor stalls, and notices Ilsen's own hesitation—a man following orders he despises. Emotional beat: the enemy revealed as another trapped person.

chapters.title: The Night the Ink Ran Out
chapters.summary: Freya's POV. Supplies fail; Freya makes ink from soot and wine and copies until her hands bleed. Noor returns from the river with a barge secured but only room for the pages, not the people. Emotional beat: the price of survival made literal—what can be saved, and what cannot.

chapters.title: The Certification
chapters.summary: Noor's POV. Summoned before Ilsen and the garrison clerk, Noor signs the certification—then, unseen, signs it in the wrong hand and date, voiding it. The forgery buys three days. Emotional beat: the courier's final betrayal of duty, performed with a steady hand.

chapters.title: Ash Forecast
chapters.summary: Freya's POV. The forgery is discovered; Ilsen orders the workshop burned that night and detains Aldous Venn. Freya sends Tomas ahead to the barge with the finished copies and goes back for her father. Emotional beat: panic sharpened into resolve; loyalty tested at the door of the fire.

chapters.title: The Burning of the Workshop
chapters.summary: Noor's POV, climax. Noor and Freya rescue Aldous from the garrison cellar as the workshop burns, the registry's originals curling in the heat. Ilsen catches them at the quay—and lets them pass, taking the blame himself, one order he refuses. Emotional beat: climax and grace; the ledger saved by a refusal.

chapters.title: Pages Delivered by Hand
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. In the burning town's chaos, Noor and Freya deliver copied pages door to door—names pressed into hands, warnings whispered, some families fleeing, some refusing to go. Emotional beat: grief and purpose braided; the work finished, imperfectly, in time.

chapters.title: The Last Page
chapters.summary: Noor's POV. On the barge, Freya discovers the final page Noor copied: their two names, entered in the registry in Noor's hand, dated the night of the confession—proof, in the republic's own format, that they existed and were promised to each other. Emotional beat: love against duty resolved into love as duty.

chapters.title: Carried
chapters.summary: Freya's POV, epilogue. Years later, in a town across the border, Freya keeps a small archive of the delivered pages and the families they saved. Noor returns from a supply run with bread and news, carrying nothing heavy. Emotional beat: quiet resolution—survival measured finally not in what was carried, but in who.
